🩸 DmC: Devil May Cry – A Rebellion Reforged 🩸
⭐ Review by a longtime Devil May Cry fan ⭐

🎮 Playtime: 400+ hours (multiple playthroughs, all difficulties)
🔁 Completed: Human to Dante Must Die + Vergil's Downfall DLC

👿💔 “Reboots are always controversial – but this one? This one tore the fanbase in half like a demon under Ebony & Ivory.” 💔👿

Let me say this upfront: I'm a HUGE fan of the classic DMC series. I grew up with the gothic style of DMC1, the relentless combat of DMC3, and the stylish chaos of DMC4. So when Ninja Theory's DmC: Devil May Cry dropped in 2013, I was ready to hate it.
But guess what? I didn’t.
I played it. I replayed it. And then I replayed it again.
And somewhere along the line... I learned to love it. 💥🖤

🎭 STORY: A REBELLION AGAINST CONTROL
This version of Dante isn’t the wisecracking pizza-gobbling half-demon rockstar from the old days. He’s more raw. More angry. More… punk.
🧑‍🎤 The world of DmC is a twisted dystopia where demons control humanity through media, finance, and sugary drinks 🍷📺💰 (Yes, I’m looking at you, Virility). It’s satire, it’s edgy, and sometimes it tries a little too hard—but it WORKS.

Dante starts out as a trash-talking orphan with no direction and ends up awakening to his heritage as the son of Sparda and Eva, discovering his humanity and learning compassion.
It’s not Shakespeare—but it’s a damn good ride.
And yes, Vergil is here too, rocking a fedora and preaching cold hard "order" like he's auditioning for a Jordan Peterson video. 🧢📚
Their final clash in the reboot is 💯 chef’s kiss—raw, emotional, and soaked in betrayal.

🧠 Story Score: 8/10

⚔️ COMBAT: A STYLISH EVOLUTION
Okay, let’s talk meat and potatoes: the combat.
Does it reach the sublime heights of DMC3 or DMC5? Not quite.
But is it fluid, tight, and addictive as hell? Absolutely. 🔥

You wield:

Rebellion (standard sword)

Arbiter (demonic axe with slow, massive hits)

Osiris (angelic scythe—fast and crowd-clearing)

Eryx (demonic fists—HULK SMASH)

Aquila (angelic throwing blades—aka "death frisbees" 🥏)

Shotguns, pistols, grapples, launchers, and of course... the twin pistols Ebony & Ivory 🔫🔫

Combat is combo-heavy and style-focused, encouraging experimentation with your entire arsenal.
And those angel/demon pull mechanics? Game changers. They turn Dante into a mid-air ballet of death, flying between enemies like a crimson tornado. 🌪️🩸

Yes, it lacks the style switch system of later games, but the weapon wheel is responsive, and the controls are buttery smooth. Add the SFX-heavy feedback, the slow-mo dodge counter, and the crunch of every hit?
You FEEL the power. 💪🎧

🕹️ Combat Score: 8.5/10

🌌 LEVEL DESIGN & VISUALS: A NIGHTMARE YOU WANT TO LIVE IN
Limbo is the star here.
Environments shift, morph, and try to kill you in real time. Floors collapse. Walls scream. Billboards lie.
It’s like fighting your way through a demon’s fever dream. 🌆🔮

Some stages are genuinely jaw-dropping:

The News Network level, with propaganda turning against you 📺

The upside-down world of Virility

The twisted realm of The Raptor where Dante is literally hated on by a demonic Alex Jones clone 😈🎙️

And yes, the final showdown with Vergil atop the fractured skyline? Cinematic GOLD.

💻 Art Direction Score: 9/10
🎨 Style is different from old DMC, yes—but it has its own gritty beauty.

🎧 SOUND DESIGN & MUSIC: HEADBANGING IN HELL
You may hate nu-metal. But damn... Combichrist and Noisia NAILED the tone. 🤘
Every battle theme pumps adrenaline directly into your veins. Boss themes are violent. Ambient tracks are haunting.

Dante’s new voice? Tim Phillips brings raw emotion, anger, and a surprising vulnerability.
Yes, the “F*** YOU” exchange with the Succubus is dumb. But other moments? Surprisingly well-acted. 🎤

🎵 Music Score: 8/10
🎙️ Voice Acting Score: 7.5/10

🤖 AI & ENEMIES: THE BAD AND THE BRUTAL
The enemy roster is decent, if not massive.
Demons have color-coded weaknesses (blue = angel, red = demon), so you have to use your full arsenal. Some hate this—I loved it.
It adds tactical depth and stops you from spamming one weapon. ⚖️🛠️

Boss fights? Mixed bag.

Hunter: Intro boss, sets the tone

Succubus: Gross but creative

Bob Barbas: PURE GOLD. Best level. Best boss. "F*CK YOU, DANTE" hits hard 😂

Mundus: Meh... anticlimactic.

Vergil fight: Actually amazing.

🧟 Enemy Design Score: 7.5/10
👾 Boss Score: 8/10

🧩 VERGIL’S DOWNFALL DLC: UNDERAPPRECIATED GEM
You get to play as Vergil, with his own move set, cutscenes, and tragic descent into madness.
He’s not as polished as in DMC4SE or DMC5, but still a solid, katana-slicing experience.
Yamato feels snappy. Teleports are satisfying. And that final twist? OOF.

DLC Score: 7.5/10
🥷 Vergil Simp Level: OVER 9000 💙

👎 CONS: WHAT DIDN’T WORK?
Dante’s early personality is too try-hard edgy.

The “F-bomb” overload feels like it’s trying to impress 13-year-olds.

Final boss is weak compared to series standards.

No style switch mechanic.

Some fans still hate it for not being “DMC enough”.

👑 FINAL VERDICT: IT’S NOT YOUR DAD’S DMC—BUT IT’S A DAMN GOOD ONE
📝 If you're a fan of pure gameplay, dark satire, and stylish violence, give this reboot a real shot.
It’s not perfect. It’s not classic Dante. But it’s bold, bloody, and stylish in its own rebellious way. 🎯💥

Even now, in 2025, this game holds up remarkably well.

🩸 Would Sparda approve? Maybe not.
😎 Would this Dante flip him off and do it anyway? Absolutely.

🎯 Final Score: 8.5/10
🔥 “Stylish as Hell” / “Smoking Slightly Sexy Style” 🔥
❤️ Loved by those who gave it a chance
🖤 Hated by those stuck in the past

🗨️ “Not in a million years would I’ve thought I’d love this Dante. But here we are. Me, Rebellion, and a whole lot of demons to slay.” 🗡️

🖤 Thanks for reading, demon slayers.
👺 See you in Limbo.

DmC Devil May Cry is an action-adventure, hack and slash game hailing all the way from the brainchilds of Ninja Theory. Being the fifth installment into the series, yet serving as a reboot, this game received a wide, negative reception from those who are fiercely loyal to the original series by Capcom, due to the rewritten character developments and story re-telling. Either way, I'm not one of those hardcore fans, as I accept this game for what it is and applaud it as its own interesting reimagination.

The game follows the protagonist, Dante; a young, rebellious and hot-headed delinquent, who has no memory of the dark and unfortunate past that had followed up to the present just after an escapade of clubbing, excessive alcohol consumption followed by a one night stand. The next morning, Dante awakens with a hangover and is briefly warned by a young, medium named 'Kat'. Speaking of the devil, Dante is subsequently fazed into 'Limbo', a place where demons are visible, malevolent and out for his own head. Skipping forward a few important scenes, unraveling lost family ties and major story plots, you pair up with the twin brother-nephilim you never thought you had and with his intelligence/propaganda governance over the public at large, along with Kat's advanced knowledge of Wiccan spellcraft, they'll plunge Dante back deep into Limbo to face off a number of demonic threats, i.e a roundabout circus fight with the baboon-faced Hunter. Taking down a Succubus, who's main job consists of influence over humanity through reproduction of the world's most popular soft drink. Firing off a middle-aged demon puppet disguised as a news reporter and even having to dance with the devil's mistress and their demonic spawn. All of this will depend on the ultimate test of encountering the all-powerful demon king, Mundus, conveyed in human form as a ruthless, billionaire tycoon, controlling the city through debt.

The game's engine is near to being absolutely perfect and intense. Playing the role of Dante, you have a strong and diverse arsenal by your side; performing savage combos by the slice of his sword, Rebellion or keeping the targeted enemies, stunned while juggling with his twin, ammoless pistols, Ebony & Ivory. As you progress through the story, you are granted more weapons, each with their own abilities and strategic modes. New to the series is the inclusion of the Devil Mode and Angel Mode; Dante's sword can change to the Osiris, a swift long-ranged scythe, whilst Devil mode allows the player to use the slower but much more powerful axe, the Arbiter. These modes also alter Dante's mobility and play style. Using Angel mode allows Dante to pull himself towards enemies and various points in each level, whilst Devil mode lets Dante pull enemies and objects towards him. With all of this aside, there are still a few more weapons to discover, but I'll leave the unaware player to discover.

It's also worthy to note checking out this games DLC; Vergil's Downfall, which allows you to play as Vergil, in his own side story, which just adds more context to satisfy those fans who crave more. I would definitely recommend getting this game around the time everything is on a special deal, as it's only worth buying at that time.

The only thing that I find a problem with this game is the fact that the game lacks a lock-on mechanic, which all previous Devil May Cry games had at it's disposal. You only lock on a specific target automatically, depending on the third person camera angle as well as being in the correct vicinity, as you can fire your guns at targets from quite a mile away if you're standing in the right place. But this also adds to some few minor problems, such as glitching out if you accidently latched onto a target, while a short cutscene is playing.

As a massive fan of the previous, original Devil May Cry games, I still stand by my consideration that this reboot is a breath of fresh air. Negatively looked down upon fans of the original series, due to the story flaws and late/conflictive character development, aswell the differences it has when compared to the original Devil May Cry games that fans cherish so much, Capcom gave their development rights to Ninja Theory for the correct reason; Their originality is absolutely sensational and has every correct notion to say that Ninja Theory delivered. I honestly prefer this game's visual style, as it's much more surreal, hollow and darker than the previous 'Anime'-esque originals, not saying I hate the originals, as I love them equally to this reboot, but in a different way. By all means, this game is both for the casual and intense gamer, so it's a win-win situation. It's a massive recommendation from me, to everyone.

[h2] The DMC Reboot We Deserved – Stylish, Crazy, and Criminally Underrated. [/h2]

I’m not really into anime or cartoons, but as a kid, I couldn’t resist watching Devil May Cry. That’s where I met Dante for the first time — not through the games, but the anime. And since the anime was based on the games (and not the other way around), Dante became, for me, that unhinged, cocky, demon-slaying lunatic who cracks dumb jokes, doesn’t care how ridiculous he seems, and still absolutely demolishes everything in his way.

After watching the anime, I went back to play the earlier DMC games… and honestly? I was disappointed. The gameplay felt clunky, and the Dante I met in the games lacked the wild energy and charm I saw in the anime. So, I put the series aside — but never forgot that version of Dante I loved so much.

[h2]Dream Come True! [/h2]
Then came DMC: Devil May Cry in 2013 — and holy hell, THIS WAS IT.
That insane, chaotic, no-filter demon hunter was finally back. From the first cutscene to the last boss fight, I was hooked. I couldn’t stop until I 100%’d the entire thing. And what made it even better?
	•	The controls were tight and fluid
	•	Combat was flashy, responsive, and stylish
	•	The combos felt like an endless playground
	•	The soundtrack? Pure fire — aggressive, energetic, and perfectly fitting the chaos
	•	And of course… Dante. Just as mad, funny, reckless, and badass as I always imagined

The game flopped because hardcore fans of the original series refused to accept the reboot. They didn’t want a version that was more accessible, more wild, more expressive. They wanted the same formula — and in doing so, they buried a title that could have opened up the DMC universe to a whole new generation.
The potential for expansion was huge. The story was bold, easy to follow, yet powerful, and the game offered tons of replayability. But the door was slammed shut.

Years later, I tried DMC5, and honestly, it didn’t hit the same. The gameplay was polished, sure — but the soul was missing. It felt like the series had locked itself into a corner, catering only to longtime fans instead of trying to evolve. The result? No continuation. No new vision. Just stagnation.

A new Devil May Cry anime dropped recently — and of course I watched it. While it started off a bit slow, by the end it delivered the same rush and madness that DMC: Devil May Cry (2013) did. That hype made me reinstall the game and replay it all over again. And wow… it still hits just as hard.

 I could play it a hundred more times and still enjoy every second.
If you’re coming into the series fresh, maybe after watching the Netflix anime, then THIS is the game you should play.
It’s accessible, fast, stylish and above all - crazy.

This is a reimagining of the Devil May Cry franchise and I have played the 4 games of the main series yet still enjoyed this title for it's own appeal. So many of the negative reviews both on here and online just seem to be bitter gamers upset that it appears like Capcom has scrapped the original series, characters they know from the original titles are seen and have altered stories/personalities/looks or whatever else they are comparing to those games. I saw the Ninja Theory Reboot as just that, a reimagining and I did enjoy the game.

Pros: 
The gameplay was just what I would expect from a hack and slash title, it felt smooth and the combos were more simplified than in many other games in the genre making the learning curve easier but diverse enough that you aren't using the exact same OP combo repeatedly. The angel and demon abilities were a nice touch needing the player to switch based on the scenario adding a unique gameplay that makes the game more intense especially on higher difficulty levels. I loved the level design throughout the game, the first few times through it was great fun exploring all the nooks and crannies in detail. The story, attitudes and personalities of characters may have been irritating and cliche throughout the game but by the end of the game it did feel like Dante & Virgil had evolved from the bratty teenage typical drama idiots into personalities that could very well match the personallities from the original series if a sequel to this game was made.

Cons:
I felt the story was almost rushed, I would have liked to see more background info on characters and lore in the game but I play a lot of RPGs so I am a bit biased there. While I did say they evolved by the game's end it was frustrating watching the childish antics of these two powerful beings acting like high schoolers for much of the game. Kat was a nice addition and it would have been nice seeing a DLC showing her and Vergils relationship in greater detail in the game itself. I didn't like Dante's look at first but it had nothing to do with the hair (after unlocking black hair Dante in DMC4 I used that for example), it was the fact his look in my opinion did't match the annoying personality but the look also evolved which was a clever way to make him likeable by the game's end. The combat difficulty of enemies was too simplistic once you figure out how to fight each new encounter (with the exception of the Vergil fight & Hollow Vergil in the DLC, those guys are cheap as on HOH & HAH). Finally the graphics were fine considering how fast paced the gameplay is but considering how recent it is I was surprised at the quality of the textures at times.

Summary:
A great hack and slash title that doesn't deserve the negative reviews, if it was an original concept I doubt 80% of those hate comments would even exist. I defintely would recommend the title for those new to the hack and slash genre, those who like a mix of fast paced gameplay with interesting enough story and love a grindy game you can play while doing something else at the same time. I would actually be curious to see a sequel to this title and I do feel it held it's own as a whole package but Ninja Theory original hack and slash Hellblade should do the genre justice without enraging the DMC fanbase again.

Back when this dropped, the horde frothed like it was the end of civilization. They bitched hardest about Dante’s hair like it personally cancelled their virgin cosplay conventions. As if the original games didn’t have him being an absolute prick to everyone. This Dante starts as a mouthy asshole, sure, but he grows. He earns the hero bit. He becomes more human than the smirking white-haired caricature (which I also love) ever managed. 

And yeah, you get the proper Dante by the end, earned, explained without a single word of clunky exposition. Finish the fucking game before you review it, you impatient goblins.

The combat? Sharp as broken glass. No lock-on, yet you hit what you mean to hit because the game actually respects your intent. Shorter arsenal, but the combos flow like they should—natural, vicious, satisfying. Guns finally feel right: Ebony & Ivory hit like they matter, the shotgun kicks righteous ass. 

None of that DMC2 screen-clearing nonsense or the pea-shooter tragedy of the others. It’s tight, readable, and fun from the jump. You don’t need 2D fighter autism to feel like a god. They even took the best ideas here and fed them straight into DMC5 like the smart thieves they were.

Platforming is the best the series has ever seen. Vergil’s DLC turns him into a beautiful, brutal storm once you chain the angel shit properly—faster and meaner than anything in 3, 4, or 5. 

The music? Combichrist murdering it. Industrial done right, not the dubstep blender-porn everyone made me fear, meaning that most people either didn't knew what dubstep was, or what industrial is. The language is grounded, funny, and human. No desperate edgelord spray of fucks every line. It just works.

Costumes? Weapon skins? All locked behind paywalls like some greedy prick is standing over the corpse of the game going “more.” The DMC3 Dante outfit clips like a cheap mod in cutscenes and you still see base Dante underneath half the time. You pay for the privilege of unlocking shit you should’ve earned by bleeding through the campaign multiple times. 

It’s the kind of cynical horseshit that Capcom does, and they were supposed to be better than them here.

Still. I bought the bundle on deep sale. Got hooked, shrugged, paid the three bucks. Because the core experience is that strong. Ninja Theory took the messy soul of the series, trimmed the fat, and made something that actually hooked me harder than most of the originals. The level design, the key/soul hunting, the secret missions that don’t feel like punishment—it’s confident, interesting, good.

Thirteen years later the haters are still crucifying it, and that’s why we’ll probably never get a sequel. Fuck ‘em. This game earned its horns. If you missed it, grab the bundle cheap and tell the echo chamber to choke on it. 

Worth every damn minute.

Scrolling through the Steam reviews, there are two things I've noticed.

Nearly all newcomers to the Devil May Cry games think this is a good game.
Nearly all Devil May Cry veterans ridicule, scorn and decry this game as an insult to the franchise.

Personally, I've played through (all the difficulties of) DMC3, and one playthrough of DMC4 (fell short of expectations), both on the PC. DMC3's difficulty was fiendishly difficult and the combat intricate, DMC4's Nero was not really interesting to play as (though Dante was decent).

Then I came to DmC. Threw myself into Nephilim (hard) difficulty at once, and could cope rather well (except with those Rages, argh). So, the veterans are right on one count, that the difficulty has been watered down significantly.

(EDIT: I have played through all difficulties on my friend's copy, and Dante Must Die mode wasn't even as hard as Son of Sparda on DMC3.)

But the gameplay itself is fun, mainly because of the PC-port controls which are pretty decent (as PC ports go). One gripe I have with DMC3/4 is that the PC controls are awkward and clunky as opposed to DmC's. Combos and such were far easier to pull off with DmC's controls, and combat felt smooth.

Story-wise, I actually prefer DmC.

Stow thy pitchforks and hear me out.

In DMC3, you have a brash, young man who has an unexplained grudge with his twin brother, who raised a gigantic pillar/castle/machine down the street from his shop. Said gigantic pillar/castle/machine was to be used to open a portal to the Demon World, and Dante set off to meet and fight his brother following a rather violent invitation. Dante proceeds to slaughter his way past tons of demons, deals with a backstabbing secondary antagonist and clashes with his brother several times before culminating in a battle in the Demon World itself. He realizes that he actually does care somewhat about his brother.

In DMC4, you have a brash young man who has an unexplained glowing demon-like arm, who arrives late to church, listens to music during a sermon and tries to leave the ceremony before a mysterious man appears and assassinates the head priest. Demons start popping up everywhere, and Nero begins his journey to track down the assassin, finding out that the church isn't as saintly as he thought, and eventually has his love interest kidnapped by the church. He then tries to save her, willing to kill all the demons and church members in his way.

In DmC, you have a brash young man who doesn't give a used fig about anything other than himself. A girl shows up, warning him about demons who have found his tracks, and manages to defeat said demons with the help of the girl. He still doesn't trust her, but gives her the benefit of the doubt, following her to her headquarters where he meets her boss, who happens to be his twin brother. He slowly finds out things about his past by a visit to his old home, and helps his brother's terrorist organization bring down the demons who are behind humanity's unknowing enslavement. Along the way, he begins to care for both his brother and the girl who helped him, moreso than his brother realizes. After they successfully defeat the Demon King, they have differing opinions and go their separate ways.

Plot-wise, DmC's is far more complex than DMC3/4.

In 3, you have an enemy castle. Go in, kill everything, deal with a secondary antagonist who obviously was going to betray everyone, and fight the predictable final boss in the form of your twin brother.

In 4, you have demons and a mysterious assassin, and you kill everything while hunting for the assassin. Then your girlfriend is kidnapped, and the people responsible for it are the ones who gave you your mission. Revenge, save your girlfriend, etc. etc. 

In DmC, there is actual character growth (only in Dante, admittedly [and to an extension, the girl]), where you have demons hunting you down, an actual backstory and a motivation to hunt down the demons themselves that goes beyond 'I have your girlfriend come and get her >:)' or sibling rivalry. 

Music-wise, I was initially apprehensive of the song choice. Dubstep/electronica is NOT my kind of thing. But as I played, I found that the pulse-pounding beats actually suited the combat very well, especially one boss fight in a strip club against a baby (no, really).

Visually, I find the over-the-top displays of Limbo tearing into the real world really interesting, as how even the city itself swears at Dante alters to impede his progress. The enemies are quite varied too, with the grunt 'Stygians', the 'Knight'-class mooks, beautiful yet deceitful 'Witch' and brutish 'Tyrant', and cool, teleporting, dual-katana-wielding ninjas to name a few.

You may disagree with me; feel free! This is merely my opinion, and if it does not sway yours, that's your call.

As a conclusion/TL;DR, I would like to make one thing very clear.

Though this is a Devil May Cry game, go into it as if you were going to play a completely different hack-and-slash game. An open mind works wonders.

(This is the same for Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance, for veterans of Metal Gear)

Before I get to the review; I want to say that the best way of playing this game is definitely with a controller, so before you purchase the game itself, make sure you have one.
I sort of have a love hate relationship with this game, as I keep progressing through the main campaign, its problems keeps dragging me back, yet its gameplay is just fun enough to keep me going until the end of the campaign. That doesn't mean the game itself is bad, though, lets start with the positives;
+ Gameplay feels fresh, fun, and fluid. With a little practice and some getting use to, you can pull off some flashy and spectacular combos that give you a sense of accomplishment 
+ The style system is great and encourages players to mix up their combos, use different weapons, and not just mash buttons
+ Limbo sequences are beautifully designed and are absolutely brilliant to play in and traverse through
+ The music fits well with the theme of the game most of the time
However, it does have its flaws, and here are some of them;
- The main story is pretty boring and generic with a few yet predictable twists, the way its delivered is also pretty uninspired, as there is even a level specifically designed as a generic exposition filler of the campaign's story
- Characters are uninteresting and aren't very well fleshed out. Dante's dialogues are corny and his jokes are a hit and miss, Vergil barely does anything throughout most of the campaign, and Kat is just a boring and forgettable side character. The same goes for the rest of the story's forgettable cast.
- Enemy designs are recycled and imo is worse than previous Devil May Cry titles
- Apart from a few interesting ones, levels are quite linear and can be short sometimes, the same goes for the entire campaign; which is a tad bit short
- Bosses are tedious and follows the same basic formula; take out its first health bar, expose its weak point, hit said weak point, take out its second health bar, expose its weak point again, rinse and repeat until it dies
- Camera issues hinder the flow of combat and can lead to a lot of frustration, especially when moving or engaging enemies in tight corridors or next to a wall
- Certain button prompts seems unresponsive and some of them are poorly implemented
If you can put the game's many flaws aside, the game works for what it is, and is a passable addition to the franchise, but I wouldn't consider it worthy of becoming a reboot of the Devil May Cry series.

Do I reccomend this game to new fans of the franchise? Yes. Do I reccomend it to old fans of the franchise? Yes, if you're willing to see what this game is, rather than what it isn't.

I had heard all the hate for this game and decided to buy it out of morbid curiosity as soon as it went on sale seeing as I have a bit of a soft spot for a few other universally hated games and the so-bad-it's-good genre in general. For about the first five chapters or so, this was a solid 3/10 and I was not at all enjoying myself. And then, as time went on, my attitude toward it slowly started to shift. I started having fun and found myself actually becoming immersed in the story instead of constantly pointing out its flaws. And then, before I knew it, I had accidentally become a fan of this game. Oops.

Sure, this is not a good Devil May Cry game. In fact, it has little if anything to do with the original series aside from the title and the names of the main characters. My biggest problem with it was that they tried to make it something it wasn't, shoehorning in DMC lore through cumbersome and unnecessary exposition dumps. If this had been its own thing, it would have been an enjoyable, albeit somewhat generic (at least where the story is concerned) action game that would have gotten decent reviews and then quietly slipped into irrelevance the way so many similar titles have. Where this game took its own creative liberties was where it really shined. One boss fight in particular (not going to spoil which) completely blew me away to the point where it now sits among my favorite boss fights of all time. Many of the gameplay elements are quite unique and are overall very fun and surprisingly polished.

My suggestion going into this game is to appreciate it on its own merit because if you separate it from all the hate it's garnered and from the franchise it tried and failed to become, you will find that there is actually quite a bit of enjoyment to be gleaned here. I almost didn't give it a chance and now, after playing through all of it, I regret that I was so heavily swayed by popular opinion.

[h1] Cмелая перезагрузка, которую не поняли, а зря [/h1] 
Когда студия разработчик Ninja Theory анонсировали перезапуск культовой серии, фанаты встретили его в штыки из-за смены образа Данте. Однако если отбросить ностальгию перед оригинальной франшизой, то перед нами — один из самых стильных, техничных и умных слэшеров своего времени, который очень дружелюбно относится к казуальным игрокам.

[h3] Почему этот ребут заслуживает внимание? [/h3]
[list]
    [*] Безупречный геймплей и плавность боев
Ninja Theory подарили игроку одну из лучших систем ближнего боя в серии на момент 2013 года. Смена четырех классических видов оружия на лету позволяет создавать невероятные комбинации, а управление с помощью геймпада (кнопки-модификаторы под большие пальцы) настолько эргономичны, что новичок быстро чувствует себя виртуозом и может быстро научиться комбинировать это оружие. 

[i] Если говорить об оружии, то у нас достаточно внушительный арсенал:[/i]
«Мятежник» — неизменный меч Данте, доставшийся от его отца Спарды, обеспечивает отличную смесь из комбинаций и атак, отлично подходит для запуска противника в небесную высь.
«Эбони и Айвори» — две сестры, два пистолета, черное и белое, хорошо помогают в сдерживании врагов на расстоянии, поддержке комбинаций и жонглировании противниками в воздухе.
«Арбитр» — демонический топор, наносящий сокрушительные удары и пробивающий щиты противников.
«Осирис» — ангельская коса для быстрых атак и расправы над толпой, быстрая и смертоносная.
«Аквилла» — ангельские сирюкены, которые помогают наносить урон на расстоянии. 
«Эрикс» — мощные демонические рукавицы, содержащие достаточно силы для парирования атак и жонглирования врагами любой тяжести.
    
[*] Гениальный и стильный дизайн уровней 
Это главная звезда происходящего на экране. Мир, где реальность буквально «вывернута» корпорациями-демонами, выглядит как ужас сюрреалиста. Уровни, где небо — это рекламный щит, города складываются как карточные домики под ногами, а телебашня изгибается под странным углом, — визуально они не устарели до сих пор. Этот грязный стиль игры запоминается надолго. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3716126520
[*] Социально-острый сюжет
В отличие от пафоса оригиналов, сценарист Алекс Гарленд (Пекло, 28 дней спустя) вписал историю в эпоху антиутопии. Данте здесь борется с глобальным заговором, долгами страны, дезинформацией через СМИ и наркотиком в простой газировке, которая управляет разумом людей. Это злое, ироничное и очень взрослое фэнтези, которое шепчет о том, что зло повсюду вокруг нас, просто мы его не замечаем. 
Хочется также отметить, что в данном ребуте переосмысленна история появление Данте и Верлигия, здесь они не демоны рожденные от человека, а Нефелимы, существа рожденные от ангела и демона, которые имеют колоссальную силу из-за своего происхождения и приводят Мундуса в состояние ужаса своей силой. И по этой причине мир демонов очень сильно хочет от них избавиться, расценивая их как угрозу своего правления над людьми. 
    
[*] Данте — живой персонаж, который заставляет к себе проникнуться.
Да, он не тот седой привлекательный дамский угодник, новый Данте (поначалу) — травмированный сирота, который прикрывает боль цинизмом. За годы игры (особенно в DLC «Vergil’s Downfall») его путь от «инфантильного алкоголика» до осознанного героя прописан куда глубже, чем кажется.
    
[*] Отсутствие «водных миссий» и платформинг «на отлично»
Крюк-кошка позволяет парить над пропастями, а демонические и ангельские рывки делают перемещение головоломкой, которую приятно решать. Здесь нет скучных забегов по коридорам — каждый уровень уникален по механике.
[/list]

[h3] Vergil’s Downfall: Погружение во тьму [/h3]
У игры есть одно дополнение Vergil’s Downfall  оно завязано на Вергилии и это не просто «ещё несколько миссий за брата», это психологический хоррор о том, как рождаются монстры. 
События начинаются сразу после финала основной игры. Вергилий, проигравший битву Данте и буквально истёкший кровью на могиле матери, проваливается в собственный ад — персональное чистилище, где ему предстоит встретиться с фантомами тех, кого он предал. И вот здесь кроется главная неожиданность подхода к персонажу. Ninja Theory могли бы сделать банальную историю о кровной мести, но вместо этого они показывают психологическое, тотальное разрушение персонажа. Вергилий предстаёт не холодным аналитиком и стратегом, а травмированным, озлобленным ребёнком, который не может простить ни брата, ни мать, ни себя. Из оружия Вергилию доступно только Ямато. Исключительно клинок и техника владения им, но это не ограничение, а чистый вызов, учитывая то, что это отвечает внешней элегантности персонажа и это добавляет не хилой сложности геймплейной части. Главная фишка — Двойник. Дьявольский Триггер здесь работает иначе, вы тратите шкалу, чтобы призвать точную копию Вергилия, которая может наносить такие же мощные удары как и оригинал. Музыка тоже меняется, уходит индастриал-метал Combichrist и электроника Noisia, теперь играет мрачный, оркестровый эмбиент подчёркивающий обречённость происходящего. Из минусов, можно отметить только продолжительность DLC, слишком уж оно короткое, чтобы насладиться. 

[b] По итогу, что мы получаем? [/b] 
DmC — дерзкий, визуально изобретальный и тактильно приятный экшен с отзывчивым управлением, глубокой, переосмысленной историей и совершенно другими персонажами. Ninja Theory создали не копию, а глубокое переосмысление, которое было предназначено именно больше для западного игрока. Если перестать сравнивать его с оригиналом 2001 года, получится мрачный, стильный и политически острый боевик с отличной музыкой (Noisia, Combichrist). Это тот случай, когда ребут действительно стал свежим дыханием франшизы и получился крутым. Рекомендую.

This is my first time playing a Devil May Cry game, with this being what introduced me to the series. Having never played any of the previous games in the series, all I knew was this being a hack and slash game and that it was a reboot of the series. I know this game received a lot of hate when it was initially released, because of it being a reboot, having a brand new Dante, and that sort of stuff. My review can't really speak on that as I haven't played any of the other games in the series. So my review will be based solely on this game itself and my experience with it. That said, I can definitely say I really enjoyed this game and had a lot of fun with it. The soundtrack is a pretty wild one, with some crazy music, but it definitely suits the atmosphere of the game and makes the battles and fights rather exciting. The atmosphere of the game was really great, as it didn't take long for me to be immersed into the world of Devil May Cry. From the level designs to the art style of the game, Devil May Cry's visuals definitely impressed me and just added to the amount of fun I was already having with the game. It also further impressed me as well. The fights themselves are smooth and fast-paced, with the music just really adding a lot to the fights. It definitely got me really into the fights. There's also a lot of stuff to do in the game as well. The main game consists of 20 missions, but it's more than that. There's lots of collectibles, side missions, and more. With storyline, I thought it was pretty good for a hack and slash adventure-action game, It definitely kept me interested until the end, and even wanting more. Fingers crossed that this game does get a sequel. But yeah, adding onto the game's content, there's definitely a lot of replay value, with the various difficulty modes of the game, which can be unlocked by completing other modes. Or going back through levels to collect missed items, find hidden secrets, and more. As I said, a lot of replay value. To be honest, I think at the beginning of the game, Dante was someone you could have mixed feelings for, but I think he had some great character development as the game progressed, developing into a hero that made me proud to have played.

Overall, I found DmC: Devil May Cry to be a great game that I had a lot of fun with until the very end, and yet still wanting more. From an awesome soundtrack to interesting storyline to impressive visuals and atmosphere, this game impressed me in many areas. I had my doubts about this game before going into it, however after giving it a chance and playing it fully through, I can definitely say my initial doubts where proven wrong. I'm glad I took the chance on this game, as I had a lot of fun with it. I've got no problem recommending this game to any of my friends. It's well worth two thumbs up from me.

As of writing this I recently started my Devil May Cry journey, have completed the HD Collection on Normal difficulty (yes, even DMC 2), in the middle of playing DMC 4 and already can't wait to get into DMC 5. But I'll be honest, after hearing and seeing so many things about this particular game I thought to myself: "Something tells me I'm gonna love this one". Lo and behold, that was exactly the case for me. And this is coming from someone who absolutely loved DMC 3.

Let's get the elephant in the room out first: yes, the story and characters are not the strongest part of this game, it is a total hit or miss when it comes to the narrative choices (especially Dante's "banter" with bosses). The best way I can describe the story is that it has a pretty strong start but loses its momentum after a while and is just overall not very well thought out. Apparently this game was originally gonna be somewhat different in its tone, more like DMC meets American McGee's Alice which would've been a much more fitting setting for a more jaded Dante, Limbo and Kat's backstory and that would've been a lot more interesting IMHO. Instead we have a delinquent Dante fighting a totalitarian demonic regime. Don't get me wrong, I eat that dystopian "man vs the system" s@#t up like a bottom feeder but unfortunately we don't spend a whole lot of time in this world to get fully invested in it. El Donte himself isn't as bad as people say but he definitely doesn't hold the candle to how amazing original Dante is. Making him and Vergil nephilim (half-demon, half-angel) is entirely pointless since angels don't play a part in the story at all. The only reason for this being a thing is that Ninja Theory probably needed a lore canon reason for the color coded gameplay. Kat is cute and precious btw.

Speaking of gameplay, my god! The combat system here has gotta be the most fluid, dynamic and satisfying it has been in the franchise so far (remember, I haven't played DMC 5 yet). The amount of weapons, abilities and their functions as well as the grappling hook are just enough to be in full control of the enemies around you. Yes, it is somewhat simpler than the original games but overall the gameplay is extremely fun regardless. Unfortunately DMC 1 called and it wants its auto lock-on back. It's not as annoying as it was in DMC 1 but could still throw you off a bit. The platforming and exploration is honestly more enjoyable than, for example, DMC 3 and 4 where I could sometimes lose my way around since no matter the mission everything is interconnected. Levels and their secrets in DMC 2013 are more linear and therefore more straightforward, built like a proper Metroidvania where you can't access certain parts without progressing through the game first (no more jumping on random pillars and ledges for free Red Orbs, sorry) which allows for a more comfortable replayability.

The art direction of this game is a gritty urban aesthetic further enhanced by Limbo's surrealism. That allowed developers to make some genuinely creative and dynamic levels and situations. Again, in the original vision for the game Limbo and enemy design would make a lot more sense but developers managed to make it work regardless.

And don't even get me started on the music! Noisia did a great job with very atmospheric score and really cool tracks for bosses (I've been listening to Hunter Demon's and Bob Barbas's themes non-stop) while Combichrist provided blood-pumping hard-rock combat music. This alone makes the game very enjoyable!

To sum it up, this "reboot" totally did not need to exist, the original Devil May Cry was already perfect the way it was. That being said Ninja Theory created a truly unique DMC experience that you may or may not like whether you are a fan of the original games or a newcomer wanting to get into the franchise. Regardless of how you feel about this game it is anything but boring (looking at you, DMC 2). And despite absolutely loving the original games I'll be a contrarian and proudly say that this is my personal favourite game in the franchise and will recommend it for at least one playthrough.

Despite it's harsh reception upon release, DmC: Devil May Cry is an interesting spin on the Devil May Cry series. Usually, we all know the standard gameplay mechanics such as DMC's styles mechanic. I.E there's different styles for different playstyles, Trickster being a style about movement, and Swordmaster about swords, or gunslinger being about gunplay, you get the picture.

DmC: Devil May Cry takes on the gameplay by doing away with that mechanic, and making the game more freestyle, instead getting rid of the style switching and just reverting to Angel and Demon weapons, which have their own neat powers (i.e demon weapons being heavier hitting, angel weapons being the opposite). The game UNIRONICALLY controls amazingly despite reeking of being an Unreal Engine 3 game, and the gameplay is surprisingly intuitive.

The soundtrack is possibly the best in the series considering this game's reputation, with Combichrist and Noisia producing most of the soundtrack. The story is surprisingly decent if you disconnect it from the DmC series itself, as this game probably would've performed way better had it not even been a DMC game.

Overall, a very fun experience and worth the money.

It's a genuinely fun game that suffers from taking on a gigantic IP. Story-wise, they'd have been better off just making their own thing. No one would have complained about the new story, they would have had more freedom with lore, there wouldn't have been that ridiculously stupid wig scene, etc. 
Old controversy aside, now that things have blown over, the game's worth a shot. Dante's a sarcastic idiot who spews one-liners like an 80s action hero, and it's great. It's not so much a masterpiece of social commentary as it is campy fun. So, since I like campy fun, I like this game. 
Gameplay-wise, it's an odd mix of 3D platformer and hack 'n' slash. I've played it on console and PC and had a much easier time with a keyboard. You'll do a lot of jumping around, even in fights, and these two aspects aren't always the most complimentary. Frankly, falling off a stage for the 10 millionth time can get aggravating. (But maybe I should give up on being fancy.) Luckily, this is somewhat made up for by the environments, which can be genuinely interesting. The stages feel like they belong in another, twisted version of reality, which is always a good time. The soundtrack is also perfect for wreaking havoc, being half the reason why this is going to become my new stress-relief game. Turns out heavy metal is a great backer for violence.
Basically, the game has entertaining ideas, some cool moments, and an interesting vibe. I went in with low expectations but actually found [i]DmC: Devil May Cry[/i] to be a pretty great game.

The graphical design, the action set-pieces and bosses, the combat, the pumping soundtrack, all of that was great. The story itself was a bit weaker but still fit with the world of [i]Devil May Cry[/i] generally. It just used modern day obsessions to play out some of the demon stories and still had the basic Dante and Vergil dynamic, but it played out in a slightly different way.

A big pro on the combat system is the Angel and Devil modes you could use for each weapon on-the-fly; add that to the ability to swap between all weapons very easily and you had quite a lot of variety. I'm actually pretty weak at this series in general, but I found this game very fun to play through. Some people in the reviews think there's too many combinations or that getting SSS combos is too difficult because of that, but I actually disagree.

I would say the weakest aspect of the game is the way its plot begins, but the gameplay starts off great right away. The further into the game, the plot becomes decent, and the gameplay keeps building up, so it's worth playing through. The controversial "joke" (which I agree is pretty dumb) is right towards the beginning of the game; but by the end of the game I think everything's pretty reasonable (and [spoiler]Dante ends up with white hair anyway[/spoiler]).

As far as the DLC, Vergil's gameplay starts out a bit weaker and slower but by the time you build him up, I actually found his combat to be even more fun. That said, the DLC levels were nowhere near as interesting, its plot was nothing special, and his combat occasionally had a glitch where his sword hit the ground and stopped certain attacks. I never had issues like that in the main game.

Overall, this game is very enjoyable to play, despite its weird outcast behavior in comparison to the rest of the series.
